references.text: The parallel text in the instructions for the breastpiece, where the twelve stones with the names of the sons of Israel are first described.
The description of the two onyx stones on the shoulder pieces with the names of the children of Israel engraved, which also represent the twelve tribes.
The list of Jacob's twelve sons who became the patriarchs of the twelve tribes of Israel, whose names were engraved on the stones.
Jacob's blessing explicitly mentions the twelve tribes of Israel.
The listing of the twelve tribes in connection with the census in the wilderness.
The new Jerusalem has twelve gates with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, an eschatological parallel to the twelve stones of the breastpiece.
The twelve foundation stones of the wall with the names of the twelve apostles, which correspond to the twelve stones on the breastpiece.
The original instruction regarding 'engraving' (28:11) is directly carried out in 39:14, emphasizing obedient adherence to God's specific requirements for the priestly equipment.
